To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) active feedback is beneficial to information retrieval; (2) diversity of documents is more important than the number of documents; (3) the best way to obtain diversity is by using a probabilistic model.
diversity-based relevance feedback can outperform the traditional relevance feedback in ad hoc IR.
diversity-based selection of feedback documents outperforms top-k selection of feedback documents, and that the diversity-based selection can be implemented with a very efficient algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new direction in ad hoc information search, i.e., active feedback, which can potentially improve the performance of information search.
the question of how to choose documents in relevance feedback to maximize the learning benefit.
the question of how to choose a subset of relevant documents for active feedback.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of a retrieval system can be improved significantly by using active feedback.
active feedback should be performed in an intelligent manner.
the diversity of documents for relevance feedback is important for active feedback.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can learn more from less feedback.
diversity-based relevance feedback is more effective than the traditional relevance feedback in ad hoc retrieval.
a retrieval system should not blindly present the top K documents for relevance feedback; instead, the system should carefully choose the documents that have the most learning benefits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diversity of feedback information is important in the active feedback process.
diversity is an important factor to consider for active feedback, and that the performance gain from using diversity is more significant than the loss from fewer relevant documents.
